title: Ensuring Bulk of New Jobs Created Will Go to Singapore Citizens and Residents, Including Those Above Age 40
what_it_is: Ensuring Bulk of New Jobs Created Will Go to Singapore Citizens and Residents, Including Those Above Age 40

sections.label: Resident employment rate 2023
sections.summary: The resident employment rate was 66.2% in 2023.

sentences.text: In 2023, our resident employment rate was 66.2%.

sections.label: Non-resident employment growth breakdown
sections.summary: Of 83,500 non-resident employment growth last year, about 18,700, or 22.4%, was from EP and S Pass holders.

sentences.text: If you take a closer look at the 83,500 non-resident employment growth last year, about 18,700, or 22.4%, was from higher-skilled Employment Pass (EP) and S Pass holders.

sections.label: Resident PMET and pass holder growth
sections.summary: Between 2013 and 2023, resident PMETs increased by 380,000 and EP and S Pass holders by 50,000.

sentences.text: Between 2013 and 2023, the number of resident PMETs increased by 380,000; and the number of EP and S Pass holders increased by 50,000.

sections.label: EP and S Pass holder totals
sections.summary: EP and S Pass holders totalled 393,700 in December 2019 and 383,900 in December 2023.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The total number of EP and S Pass holders was 393,700 in December 2019 – this was the year before COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And we ended last year with 383,900 – this was in December 2023.

sections.label: EP and S Pass share of workforce
sections.summary: Total EP and S Pass holders remain about 32% of the overall workforce, with focus on enabling Singaporeans' job choices.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, really, if you want to compare the type of jobs that Singaporeans would prefer to be in and, as I have shared earlier on, our focus is on enabling, helping and facilitating every Singaporean who wants to choose a particular job or role, will be able to do so.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, look at that particular sector and for the record, in terms of the total EP and S Pass holders, it is still about 32% of our overall workforce.

sections.label: Jobs statistics separating citizens and PRs
sections.summary: Mr Leong is asked if his conclusions are incomplete while jobs statistics do not separate Singaporeans from permanent residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Leong, I would really like you to ask the supplementary question.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, does he agree that his conclusions are not complete, as long as the jobs statistics do not separate the Singaporeans from the permanent residents (PRs), because there are these changes within the resident employment that are not completely transparent to us?
